# v0.9.2 - Times Survive a Restore, `--force-with-lease` Works, and a Directory the Tool Cannot Read No Longer Vanishes From the Snapshot

## What's Changed in v0.9.2

Two more rounds of independent review went over the snapshot tool: Opus twice on the code (the second
time on code written for this release), and GLM-5.3 and Gemini on the specification. Every finding that
reproduced is fixed with a test that fails without the fix. The suite is 1049 tests; the tool and helper
changes were also run on Linux (Debian under WSL) and against a real Seafile server (CE 13.0.28) in a
scratch library.

### The one that mattered most

- **A directory the tool could not read was silently missing from the snapshot.** `git add` prints a
  warning for a directory it cannot open and exits 0, so everything under it was absent and the run
  reported success. The run now stops and names the directory; `--exclude` leaves it out on purpose.

### Added

- **Modification times of git-stored files are restored.** A snapshot that pushes to a `seafile://` remote
  records them in `.seafile-payload/mtimes.json` and `--restore` puts them back (payload files already
  carried theirs). `--record-mtimes` / `--no-record-mtimes`; an explicit choice is remembered; a run with
  nothing typed follows the last snapshot. Touching a file without changing it still makes no new snapshot.
- **`git push --force-with-lease`** is supported: a push may rewrite history over exactly the value you
  saw, and is refused as `stale info` if the remote moved. Updates, deletions and `--dry-run`.
- **A fetch no longer advertises half a repository.** A refs directory that its parent listed and that then
  answers 404 is retried once and then an error.
- **macOS network mounts** are recognised by the clock probe.

### Fixed in the snapshot tool

- A restore overwrote and then removed a real git file named `<payload file>.part`, and certified the tree.
- A manifest path through a link to `.git` (`tool/hooks/pre-commit`) passed the "inside the destination"
  check; a hostile manifest could fill the disk before its sizes were compared.
- A share whose clock ran 2 to 5 s behind kept a stale hash (the noise floor was wider than the racy
  window); a share that could not be probed fell back to the machine's clock; a same-size edit that put the
  old mtime back was trusted. The cache key now holds the device and the inode change time, unprobed
  shares and other devices get a one-hour margin, and whole-second mtimes are trusted (twice the margin)
  instead of being re-read on every run of a FAT or HFS+ volume.
- `--no-embedded-repos` after a capturing run wrote a gitlink naming the vault's own commit; a repository
  inside a repository crashed the run; one with no commit failed every run; a junction that is itself a
  repository was followed out of the tree.
- `--payload-gc` decided from a listing that could have skipped a branch (so its objects looked unused),
  and from a decision minutes old. The listing is strict and the refs are read again before the first
  deletion.
- A pid recycled by an unrelated process blocked every later snapshot on Windows.
- The weekly report copied the whole vault into the temporary directory and ran on a vault's first run.
- A manifest path using a code point HFS+ ignores was accepted; flags that would be ignored are refused.

### Documentation

- Corrected: the source is "never written to" (a probe file on a network share), objects are "never
  overwritten", a payload vault can snapshot offline (it cannot), `--payload-verify` covers every snapshot
  (the newest only), and 0.9.1's claim that the conflict-copy warning missed dotted refs (measured on a
  real server: it did not).
- Stated: tags must be pushed to be seen by retention; the manifest is one line; a 0.8.8 machine restores a
  payload vault's git tree only, without a warning.

### Upgrading from 0.9.1

- A directory that cannot be read now stops the run: a scheduled job that had been skipping one will fail
  until it is made readable or excluded.
- `--payload-gc` stops, deleting nothing, if a ref cannot be read or a push landed while it decided.
- A vault gets `.seafile-payload/mtimes.json` on its next pushing run (about 60 bytes a file; about 1.5 MB
  compressed at 100,000 files, uploaded whole each time anything changes). `--no-record-mtimes` opts out.
- No file format changed; 0.9.1 vaults and remotes are read as before.

### Known gaps

- The times record is one blob, rewritten whole when any file changes (sharding it is a format change).
- A nested repository's history, and directory times, are not captured.
- macOS (NFD names, HFS+, `utime` on symlinks) is covered by reasoning and CI, not by a Mac here.

The full list, with measurements, is in `CHANGELOG.md`.
